problems.problem: All text uses Arial, a neutral grotesque with no luxury character; reference campaigns (Tom Ford, Armani Privé) pair a serif or refined logotype with wide-tracked caps. The title/subtitle column is a plain left-aligned stack with large uneven gaps (logo y220, title y310, subtitle y420), reading as a layout placeholder rather than a designed typographic block.

The enlarged base crop (contact_detail_crop 128,1105–671,1355) shows the bottle base resting on the surface with only a very faint darkening beneath; the contact shadow (opacity 0.35, blur 10) is too weak and diffuse for a glossy dark bottle on a light matte floor. No floating is present, but grounding is under-articulated — soft reflection/stronger contact occlusion is needed to match luxury reference lighting.

The bottle occupies 59% of canvas height (correct hero range), but the right text column sits vertically compressed in the upper third while the lower right two-thirds is empty wine-red floor; the layout is balanced only by accident, and no secondary element (rule, texture, deco accent, price) anchors the lower right. decoration is disabled though spec reserves a gold accent slot.

The flat paper wall + window-frame diagonal shadow concept is competent but generic; references integrate a sculptural thematic prop (fig, lacquer splash, sandalwood). The campaign lacks any element expressing Tobacco Vanille's warmth beyond color, so concept strength trails the reference set.

Compared to the provided references, the poster lacks typographic refinement (font choice), a signature compositional device, and a subtle material interplay; it reads as a competent draft rather than a professionally resolved campaign.

changes.value: Deep wine-red matte seamless studio cyclorama wall flowing into a matching seamless floor, one crisp architectural diagonal shadow cast across the upper wall, a gentle warm amber glow rising from the lower right foreground like lamplight through amber glass, smooth uncluttered center, uniform broad soft frontal illumination, realistic physical studio environment photograph
